transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Thursday, November 19. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Watch: Man attempts to enter Delhi airport without documents, CISF detains him. An incident occurred at Delhi Airport where a man attempted to enter Terminal-3 without valid travel documents. CISF personnel quickly apprehended him at the entry gate, preventing access. The individual was later handed over to Delhi Police for questioning. Officials reported recovering IDs and educational certificates from the man's backpack. Punjab bridge collapses on Patiala-Sangrur road, two trucks plunge into canal. An iron bridge over the Bhakra Canal in Punjab collapsed with two trucks on it, which fell into the structure. One of the trucks caught fire shortly after the collapse, resulting in emergency response efforts. Fire brigade personnel worked swiftly to control the blaze and prevent further spread of the fire. Police teams arrived at the scene to manage the situation as onlookers gathered around the bridge. Row erupts as Sena neta tears photo showing Bal Thackeray hitting effigy. Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders criticized Shaina N C for allegedly disrespecting Bal Thackeray's image during a protest. This incident involved her tearing a page from Sonia Gandhi's memoir featuring a photograph with Thackeray. Eknath Shinde supported Shaina's claim that the focus was on Mani Shankar Aiyar's face. Congress condemned the actions, arguing that tearing pages cannot alter historical narratives. Airbnb CEO praised Chinese AI models; US may ask to share china preference. In October 2025, Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky highlighted that the company uses Alibaba's Qwen AI models for customer service. The Trump administration is considering a plan for companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models. This proposal aims to discourage reliance on Chinese technology while avoiding regulatory backlash. Members of Congress have initiated investigations into American firms that utilize Chinese AI technologies. 'Wasn't permissible for bench headed by Amanullah': CJI pulls cases from SC judge. CJI Surya Kant withdrew two cases from the bench headed by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah, averting a potential religious controversy. Coyote may be first to cross $114m California wildlife bridge before opening. In an exciting development, a coyote has been spotted utilizing a newly constructed wildlife bridge spanning California's US 101 Freeway. This innovative structure is designed to reconnect fragmented habitats caused by highways and urbanization. Researchers are actively observing wildlife interactions with the bridge through remote cameras, aiming to enhance the migration of various species, such as mountain lions and deer. Cummins under pressure as Bancroft's claims trigger calls for captaincy review. Cameron Bancroft's recent statements have raised serious doubts regarding Pat Cummins's credibility as Test captain. Bancroft revealed that many team members knew about the ball-tampering plot during the 2018 South Africa tour. Cummins has consistently denied any knowledge of the incident, despite the mounting public scrutiny. An independent forum has been established by Cricket Australia for players to share their experiences. Health of states: Bihar per capita spend lowest, Sikkim's highest. There are wide regional disparities on what govt spends on healthcare. Assam class 10 girl Rakhi Rabha wins President's Scout award. In November 2026, Rakhi Rabha, a dedicated Class 10 student from Thengapara, proudly earned the President Scout Award. This accolade underscores her unwavering dedication to scouting, overcoming the challenges posed by her rural upbringing. Her outstanding performance in both the President Scout examination and the Scheduled Tribe Olympic Talent Search Programme has caught the eye of local leaders, motivating her peers. Warm California seas reveal about 10 fish species never recorded in state before. The rising ocean temperatures along California's Pacific coast are attracting a variety of new fish species, surprising local fishermen with the uncharted marine life. Sightings include whale sharks, giant manta rays, and an unusual orange fish captured in Los Angeles. Experts warn that such alterations could disrupt existing marine ecosystems, threatening the vital kelp forests and the organisms that inhabit them in the long run. Anthropic researcher sends 'AI warning', says the technology can soon bully humans. Tao Lin, a researcher at Anthropic, has warned about the imminent rise of artificial intelligence capabilities. He emphasizes that AI will soon surpass human competencies across various fields and conflicts. Lin suggests that people should view AI not merely as a tool but as a potential adversary. He predicts that this shift will create significant power imbalances in society.
